title.en: Practice: Interpersonal skills: listening and responding
title.hi: अभ्यास: अंतर-वैयक्तिक कौशल: सुनना और उत्तर देना

section: Practice (written by us, not from a UPSC paper): Interpersonal skills: listening and responding

en.stem: A supervisor explains a new procedure to a team and wants to be sure it has been understood. What is the best way?
options: Ask: is that clear?
Repeat the explanation more loudly
Ask a team member to describe the steps in their own words
Put up a notice on the board
en.why: Only the third option produces feedback that shows what was understood. Is that clear usually draws a yes whether or not it is.

en.stem: A citizen says: 'This is the third time I have come for this certificate.' Which reply shows the best listening?
options: 'You have had to come three times and it is still not done. Let me see what is holding it up.'
'Many people have to come several times.'
'Please do not raise your voice.'
'You should have brought all the papers the first time.'
en.why: The first reply says back the fact and the frustration and then moves to action. The others dismiss, correct or blame.

en.stem: While a colleague describes a difficulty, you keep typing and say 'go on, I am listening'. The colleague stops talking. What best explains this?
options: The colleague had finished
The colleague dislikes computers
Your words were unclear
Your manner contradicted your words, and the colleague believed the manner
en.why: When words and manner disagree, people go by the manner. Typing signals that attention is elsewhere.

en.stem: An urgent change in the time of a meeting two hours from now has to reach six officers. Which channel is most suitable?
options: A notice on the office board
A telephone call to each, followed by a short written message
A letter by post
Mention it at the meeting itself
en.why: The message is urgent, so it needs a channel that reaches at once and gives immediate confirmation; the written message keeps a record.

en.stem: Which of the following is an example of paraphrasing?
options: 'I know exactly how you feel.'
'That happened to me too, last year.'
'So the pump was repaired in June, and it failed again within a week. Is that right?'
'You should write to the head office.'
en.why: Paraphrasing says back the substance and invites correction. The others claim understanding, turn to oneself, or give advice.

en.stem: A subordinate asks for leave during a week when the office is short of staff, and you cannot grant it. Which reply is assertive?
options: 'I cannot spare you that week because two people are already away. Can we look at the week after?'
'All right, take it, we will manage somehow.'
'You people always want leave at the wrong time.'
'I will see.'
en.why: The first reply is plain about the refusal, gives the reason and offers a way forward. The second is passive, the third aggressive, and the fourth avoids an answer.

en.stem: A junior has submitted a report with the figures for one month missing. Which feedback is most useful?
options: 'You are careless.'
'This is not good enough.'
Say nothing and add the figures yourself
'The March figures are missing from the table. Please add them and send it back today.'
en.why: Useful feedback is about the act, specific, and says what is wanted. The first labels the person, the second is vague, and the third gives no feedback.

en.stem: An officer explains a scheme to villagers using the abbreviations and terms of the department. The villagers nod but later do not apply. What was the main barrier?
options: The villagers were not interested
The language used was not that of the listeners, and no feedback was sought
The meeting was too short
The scheme was a poor one
en.why: The failure is at the step of putting the idea into words the receiver knows, and nodding was taken for understanding.

en.stem: Which of the following is a mark of poor listening?
options: Asking the speaker what happened next
Waiting for the speaker to finish
Preparing your reply while the other person is still speaking
Saying back the main point
en.why: Attention given to one's own reply is attention taken from the speaker. The other three are parts of good listening.

en.stem: A farmer whose crop-loss claim has been rejected under the rules is angry. Which reply shows empathy without giving a false promise?
options: 'Do not worry, I will get it approved.'
'Rules are rules.'
'There is no point in being angry with me.'
'I can see this is a hard blow after a bad season. The claim was rejected because the survey shows a loss below the limit. You can appeal within the time allowed, and I will explain how.'
en.why: The fourth reply acknowledges the feeling, gives the reason, and names a real next step. The first promises what the officer cannot deliver.

en.stem: Which statement about empathy is correct?
options: It is understanding and acknowledging another person's point of view and feeling
It means agreeing with whatever the other person wants
It means feeling sorry for someone from a distance
It is useful only in personal life
en.why: Empathy is understanding from the other's side and showing it. It does not require agreement, and it differs from pity.

en.stem: You have to tell a colleague that a proposal they worked hard on has not been accepted. What is the best way?
options: Send a one-line message
Tell them in person and in private, give the reasons, and say what could be taken forward
Let them hear it from others
Announce it at the staff meeting
en.why: Unwelcome news is best given directly, privately and with reasons, through a channel that allows the other person to respond.

en.stem: Consider these statements: 1. Communication is complete when the message has been sent. 2. Tone of voice can change the meaning of the same words. Which is correct?
options: 1 only
Both 1 and 2
2 only
Neither 1 nor 2
en.why: Communication is complete only when the receiver understands, so statement 1 is wrong. Statement 2 is right: manner is part of the message.

en.stem: In a discussion, a colleague disagrees sharply with your suggestion. Which response is most likely to keep the discussion useful?
options: 'You never agree with anything I say.'
Withdraw the suggestion at once
Stop speaking for the rest of the meeting
'Tell me which part you think will not work, and why.'
en.why: The fourth response asks for the substance of the objection and keeps the exchange on the matter. The first attacks the person; the second and third give up one's own point.

en.stem: An instruction must be followed exactly by many offices and may be referred to months later. Which form of communication is most suitable?
options: A telephone call to each office
A written order in plain words, with a contact for questions
A remark at a meeting
Word of mouth through visiting staff
en.why: Where exactness and a lasting record are needed, writing is the right channel; the contact allows feedback.
